root_cause: The navigation controller uses closure variables (currentFocus, dataFeedback) that become stale when the suggestion list is re-rendered. The keydown listener is attached only once (via a guard flag) but retains references to the initial render's state. When the user types additional characters, the list updates but the listener's closure still holds the old focus index and results, causing incorrect aria-selected assignment and Enter selection.
repair_strategy: Store navigation state (currentFocus, dataFeedback) on the config object (the autoComplete instance) so they persist across renders and are always current. Reset config.currentFocus to -1 and update config.dataFeedback each time navigate is called. Modify the inner functions to read/write these config properties. Keep the guard flag to attach the keydown listener only once.
expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard navigation will correctly track focus and active descendant across list re-renders, ensuring that pressing Enter selects the currently highlighted suggestion.
functional_risks: If a custom navigation function is provided, it will not benefit from the shared state on config; it must manage its own focus tracking.

The config object now has additional properties (currentFocus, dataFeedback, _navigationListenerAttached) which could theoretically clash with other code, but this is unlikely given the limited scope.
verification_requirements: After typing 'b', pressing ArrowDown twice, typing 'l', pressing ArrowDown once, and pressing Enter, the input value must be 'Blackberry'.
Repeatedly opening and closing the suggestion list must not accumulate multiple keydown listeners.
If a custom navigation function is supplied via config.resultsList.navigation, it should continue to work as expected.
